identity: An in-page task widget presents facts in one view and asks the user to remember them when completing a later view.

scenarios.name: code
scenarios.screen: The first step of a request flow shows a reference code beside a Next button. The code entry field and confirmation screen are not visible.
never: A code entry field on the first step.
The confirmation screen open at the start.
All flow steps displayed at once.

arrangements.text: The step title sits above the reference code, with Next beside the code.
The step title sits to the left of a row containing the reference code and Next.

scenarios.name: count
scenarios.screen: A scrollable table shows the first batch of a longer list of about 50 rows. An empty answer box and its confirmation button sit outside the list; later rows are not yet loaded into view.
never: The full list visible at once.
A displayed total for the matching rows.
A filled answer box at the normal start.
A separate page for later rows.

arrangements.text: The column headings and scrollable rows sit above the answer box.
The scrollable table sits to the left of the answer box.

scenarios.name: paginate
scenarios.screen: The first results page shows about five rows, a selection button for each row, and controls for moving among roughly four pages. No row is selected, and no other results page is visible.
never: Rows from every results page shown together.

arrangements.text: The result rows run down the page with each selection button beside its row; the page controls sit below the rows.
The page controls sit above the result rows, with selection buttons aligned in a column to their right.

scenarios.name: crossref
scenarios.screen: Tabs lead to two people’s records, an Order record, and a form. The first source tab is open with labeled facts; the form’s fields are not on screen.
never: All source records and the form visible together.
The form already filled at the normal start.
A popup containing the source values.
A separate browser page for each tab.

arrangements.text: The tabs run across the top, with the open record’s labeled facts beneath them.
The tabs form a column on the left, with the open record’s labeled facts on the right.

scenarios.name: compare
scenarios.screen: A catalog list shows the names of about five products and a View button for each. No product detail is open or chosen; prices, ratings, delivery times, and colours appear only in detail views.
never: A product detail view open at the normal start.
Prices or ratings beside products in the list.

arrangements.text: Product names run down the list, with each View button beside its name.
Product names occupy a left column, with their View buttons aligned in a right column.
